title: The wager — twenty thousand at Baring's
learning_goal: Know the fictional trigger, the six names, £20,000 at Baring's, and the deadline; feel the click of a plan.

narration.script: Evening, at the club. Fogg and five friends sit down to whist, the card game they play nightly. In the novel — only in the novel — a thief has robbed the Bank of England of fifty-five thousand pounds. The Daily Telegraph newspaper has done the sums: the world can now be crossed in eighty days. That talk becomes a wager. Andrew Stuart, an engineer, bets four thousand pounds it can't be done. Fogg stakes twenty thousand — half his fortune — that it can: 'eighty days or less'. Look at the card: six names, Stuart first, Fogg last. Due back 'in this very room of the Reform Club, on Saturday, the 21st of December, at a quarter before nine p.m.' Exactly eighty days — and it really was a Saturday. Fogg's motto: 'The unforeseen does not exist.' Fogg's bank, Baring's, fell in 1995. The wager has outlived the bank.

variants.clear: Evening, at the club. Fogg and five friends play whist, their card game, like every night. In the story — only in the story — a thief has stolen fifty-five thousand pounds from the Bank of England. And a newspaper, the Daily Telegraph, has counted: you can now go around the world in eighty days. At the table, this becomes a bet. Andrew Stuart, an engineer, bets four thousand pounds that it cannot be done. Fogg bets twenty thousand pounds — half his money — that it can. Look at the card: six names. Stuart first, Fogg last. Fogg must be back in this same room on Saturday, the twenty-first of December, at a quarter to nine at night. Exactly eighty days. It really was a Saturday. Fogg's motto: 'The unforeseen does not exist.' Fogg's bank, Baring's, closed in 1995. The bet has outlived the bank.
